challenges.name: retry-repair-fallback-evidence
challenges.title: Retry, repair or give up? Read the hint service log
challenges.description: Two statements on real output of the CodeDev hint service: a repair request after a schema error, and a retry loop that met a 401.

questions.question:
Hint service log, one hint request (fake model in staging, token counts from the provider's usage field):
14:21:07.412 hint req=h_51c2 call=1 kind=hint   messages=2 input_tokens=2318 output_tokens=64 validation=invalid errors=["level: must be 1, 2 or 3"]
14:21:08.020 hint req=h_51c2 call=2 kind=repair messages=2 input_tokens=131  output_tokens=41 validation=valid

The repair request that was sent as call 2:
[system] Your previous answer did not match the schema {"level": 1 | 2 | 3, "hint": "<at most 300 characters>"}. Return only the corrected JSON object.
[user]   Previous answer:
         {"level": "two", "hint": "Check which branch of your ternary runs for a sum of 600000."}
         Errors:
         - level: must be 1, 2 or 3

Statement: "Call 2 cost about 6% of the input tokens of call 1 because the repair request carried only the invalid answer and the validator's error, not the system prompt, the failing test and the learner's code again."
questions.explanation: True. 131 input tokens against 2318 is about 6%. The repair request has two short messages: the repair instruction with the schema, and the invalid answer plus the exact error from validateHint. That is all the model needs to fix a shape problem: the hint text is already there, only the level is wrong. The common mistake is to append the repair to the whole conversation (system prompt, learner code, first answer, repair), which pays for the learner's code a second time on every repair and gives the model more text to get wrong.

False. A 401 says the credentials are wrong; the same request with the same key gets the same answer half a second later, so every hint request now costs three calls and 1.5 s of waiting before the learner sees a 500. A limit and backoff make a retry cheaper, not useful. Classify first: retry only transient failures (429, 502, 503, 504, timeouts), and for 400/401/403 return the fallback hint at once and raise an alert, because a human has to fix the key. The misconception is that a bounded retry is harmless for any error.

challenges.name: retry-repair-fallback
challenges.title: Retry, repair & fallback for the AI hint
challenges.description:
The CodeDev AI hint must always give the lesson page something it can render. Write getHint(req, llm, clock, opts):

1. Send hintMessages(req) with llm.complete(messages).
2. If complete() throws an LlmError with a transient status (429, 502, 503 or 504) and fewer than opts.maxRetries retries were used in this getHint call, await clock.sleep(opts.baseDelayMs * 2 ** (n - 1)), where n is the number of this retry counted over the whole call (1, 2, 3 ...), then send the same messages again. Any other status (400, 401, 403 ...), or a transient one with no retry left, ends with the fallback and reason "error <status>".
3. Check a reply with validateHint(reply.text). No errors: return the parsed hint with source "model" (answer to the first request) or "repair" (answer to a repair request). Errors and fewer than opts.maxRepairs repairs sent: send repairMessages(reply.text, errors) - only those two messages, not the original conversation - and check that reply the same way. Errors and no repair left: fallback with reason "invalid output".
4. The fallback is FALLBACK_HINT with source "fallback"; reason is null when the hint came from the model.
5. Return calls (every call to complete, including those that threw) and inputTokens / outputTokens (sums of reply.usage over the replies that came back).

The test runner replays a script on a fake model (no real LLM is called) and a fake clock, then prints every call (time, kind, messages, tokens sent, outcome), your result line and the hint. Input: { options: { maxRetries, maxRepairs, baseDelayMs }, request, script }.
hints: Three different things can happen on each call: it throws a transient error, it throws a permanent error, or it returns text that may or may not pass validateHint. Which counter does each case use up, and which messages does the next call send?

Look at what you pass to llm.complete after an invalid reply: repairMessages(reply.text, errors) replaces the messages, it is not appended to them. Then look at where you increase calls: before the try, so a call that throws is counted too.

A similar loop on other data: an image service that retries 'busy' with waits of 200 and 400 ms, and on a 'blurry' result sends one 'sharpen' request with only that image, then gives up with a placeholder. One loop, two counters (retries, sharpen requests), each checked before it is used, and the placeholder returned from every exit that is not a success.
